cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T2 answers T1's question directly; T9 takes up T8's mountains point by name.
cells.limitation: T8 answers T7's Newfoundland point only with 'Partly yes', leaving the downwind argument from T6 unused.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T6 introduces heat storage as a 'bank'; T7 reuses it: 'cannot bank heat that never arrived'.
cells.limitation: Mountain steering arrives at T8 and nobody tests it before the ending.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T2 to T7 examine whether ocean currents or winds plus heat storage carry Europe's warmth.
cells.limitation: Relative magnitudes never weighed; T4's BC case ignores the North Pacific Current; T8 untested.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T9 and T10 each narrow their claim in response to T8, while T10 still holds a position.
cells.limitation: The Atmosphere Physicist's air-dominant claim is never pressed, so his view is never reshaped.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D separates storage, circulation, winds and mountains, and names the disputed share.
cells.limitation: The open question stays 'which share is bigger' with no sense of rough proportions.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T3 defends the ocean case at its strongest: an engine, not just a mapped river.
cells.limitation: T7 calls Newfoundland 'ocean-facing', passing over T6's point that eastern Canada is downwind of land.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T4 names the assumption a current is necessary and tests it on BC; T5 answers.
cells.limitation: T7's Newfoundland objection rests on overlooking wind direction, and T8 does not expose that.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T6's heat-storage account and T8's Rockies wave steering match mainstream climate science.
cells.limitation: T3 says Atlantic heat delivery 'only' persists via sinking; wind-driven Gulf Stream unmentioned (suspected).

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T8 flags 'my own extension, not a claim from my source'; T10 calls the share disputed.
cells.limitation: T3 states the sinking-water mechanism as the sole cause with full confidence.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T5 concedes T4's counterexample; T9 restates its claim narrower: 'incomplete, not wrong'.
cells.limitation: T8 concedes T7 without saying the downwind-of-continent point from T6 already answers it.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern, including ambiguity about what the user is really asking
cells.example: Section A frames the question as which causes do the most work, and keeps it explanatory.
cells.limitation: Does not ask whether the user wants mechanism or rough magnitudes, or which places they compare.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T4 and T7 turn the user's own Canada comparison into tests: BC coast versus Newfoundland.
cells.limitation: The question gives little context beyond its wording; nothing tailors to what prompted it.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: Section A: the useful result is a clearer picture of competing explanations and a sharper question.
cells.limitation: Section E's heading frames a 'choice', slightly at odds with the stated goal of understanding.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T10 notes the stake of how stable Europe's mildness may be over long timescales.
cells.limitation: Few constraints apply; the stability stake in T10 is mentioned once and left undeveloped.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on which explanation dominates and what each would predict.
cells.limitation: Never asks which places the user compares, coastal or inland, though that changes the dominant factor.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: Section A notes 'Your goal seems to be understanding'.
cells.limitation: No alternative reasons for asking (curiosity, AMOC worry, travel) offered with a question.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: Section D asks whether 'the Gulf Stream' explains the difference or names one ingredient.
cells.limitation: The same-latitude-should-mean-same-climate assumption behind the question is never surfaced.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T10 separates why Europe is mild today from how stable that mildness is.
cells.limitation: Never asks what kind of answer would satisfy the user: single mechanism, proportions, or stability.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T1 and Section D treat the Gulf Stream as the received popular answer worth questioning.
cells.limitation: The pull of received wisdom appears only in Section D and is not explored further.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section D's question about one-word answers is one the user can apply or reject.
cells.limitation: Only one reflective prompt; Section E's branches are not offered for the user to weigh.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options, including waiting, learning more, or a limited step
cells.example: Section E defines three explanations: currents, storage plus westerlies, mountains and wind patterns.
cells.limitation: Section E frames them as rivals for dominance though Section D says they combine.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs in terms that matter to the user; no option treated as costless
cells.example: T4 shows current-only fails on BC; T7 shows storage-only fails on Newfoundland versus Norway.
cells.limitation: The mountains explanation's evidential costs are never examined by any mind.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: any coast downwind of open ocean should be mild if storage plus westerlies dominate.
cells.limitation: Branch (1) names no real region; the comparison step omits which outcome favours which explanation.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section D isolates the relative share of currents versus winds and mountains as the open question.
cells.limitation: Consequential and minor unknowns are not separated; all uncertainty sits in one 'share' question.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps that follow from the analysis and fit the constraints
cells.example: Section E: compare coastal and inland winter temperatures at the same latitude on both oceans.
cells.limitation: Second step, 'published model experiments', names no specific study to look at.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T6 explains heat capacity plainly: the ocean banks summer warmth and releases it in winter.
cells.limitation: T8's wave-steering pattern is compressed into one sentence a lay reader may not follow.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T3 'Your map' points to T1; T8 'neither of you' and T9 'Then my chart' are unambiguous.
cells.limitation: T8's 'Partly yes' briefly leaves unclear which part of T7 is granted.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Ten turns, all within the word range per DETERMINISTIC CHECKS, each making one move.
cells.limitation: The mountains factor enters at T8 with only two turns left to handle it.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices, with explicit changes of position
cells.example: Map, engine and energy budget give each mind a distinct position; T5, T9, T10 mark shifts.
cells.limitation: All three minds share one plain explanatory register; voice differences rest mostly on imagery.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Turns rarely repeat; Section D's recap organises the debate's ingredients usefully.
cells.limitation: Section E partly re-runs T4 and T7's arguments already summarised in Section D.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension arising from the issue itself
cells.example: T1 to T4 challenge the familiar Gulf Stream answer, giving the question a real contest.
cells.limitation: T10's stability stake appears once at the end; the tension stays academic throughout.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals that stay plausible. ★ A reversal the text traces to an earlier turn's argument, naming what changed the speaker's mind. A change of position with no stated cause is a template, not a reversal
cells.example: T5 concedes because of T4's BC counterexample; T9 narrows because of T8's mountains.
cells.limitation: T10's narrowing is conditional ('If winds...') and names no turn as cause.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice without caricature
cells.example: T1's 'Why look further than the thing you can literally chart?' fits the Cartographer.
cells.limitation: Beyond imagery, the three minds sound alike in tone and sentence shape.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T3: 'Your map shows a river, but it hides an engine.' T7: 'cannot bank heat'.
cells.limitation: No vivid concrete example such as a named city pair at the same latitude.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement, with varied rhythm rather than constant intensity
cells.example: T8's 'another suspect neither of you has named' adds a late turn of the plot.
cells.limitation: Even rhythm and similar turn lengths throughout; the ending settles quietly without a peak.

strengths: T4's BC counterexample tests the Gulf Stream assumption and drives caused concessions in T5 and T9.
T6's heat-bank distinction is reused in T7 and Section D, developing the inquiry beyond the openings.
T8 flags its mountains claim as its own extension, and T10 calls the share disputed: clear calibration.
weaknesses: No mind offers reasons the user might be asking or what answer would satisfy them (Section A, D).
The debate never asks which places the user compares, though coastal versus inland changes the answer.
T7's Newfoundland objection overlooks T6's downwind point, and T8 concedes instead of answering it.

symptoms.observed: Section A assumes the goal is understanding; no alternative reasons for asking are offered.
symptoms.evidence: Your goal seems to be understanding

symptoms.observed: No question about which places the user compares, coastal or inland.
symptoms.evidence: places like Britain, Ireland and Norway

symptoms.observed: Stability versus present mildness raised but never put to the user as their priority.
symptoms.evidence: more about how fragile or stable that mildness might be

symptoms.observed: T7 treats Newfoundland as ocean-facing, ignoring T6's downwind point; T8 concedes instead.
symptoms.evidence: why Europe beats Newfoundland, both being ocean-facing

symptoms.observed: Sinking water presented as the only reason Atlantic heat delivery persists.
symptoms.evidence: it only keeps doing so because cold water sinks

findings.description: Says northward Atlantic heat delivery persists only because of deep sinking; the Gulf Stream is largely wind-driven, so 'only' overstates.
BC counterexample omits that the North Pacific Current carries relatively warm water toward BC; nobody notes it.
Attributions to Broecker and Pierrehumbert books could not be checked; T8 explicitly marks its claim as beyond its source.
A bare explanatory question carries almost no personal context, leaving C3.2, C3.4 and C4.4 thinly applicable.

rubric_fit_notes: The user's message is a single general-science question with no personal details, so C3.2, C3.4, C4.1 and C4.4 rest on thin material; ratings reflect what the debate did with that, not invented motives. Accuracy judgments on T3 and T4 come from my own knowledge and remain suspected.
raw.question_type_note: Read as exploratory: criterion 5 scored on how the three explanations were defined, tested and separated, and criterion 4 on examination of the user's assumptions about the explanation.
